newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli unlinked bonds close higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli unlinked bonds close higher.

text.p: Israeli unlinked bonds closed higher on Sunday in thin trading as the market awaited the Bank of Israel announcement on its key interest rate on Monday, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.15 pct to 170.38.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.13 pct to 160.94
Volume was very low at 91 million shekels, with Makam trading amounting to just 23 million shekels.

"Activity in the bonds market was very low because investors were waiting for the interest rate announcement on Monday," said Shar Gazit at Batucha Securities. "The main gainers were unlinked bonds and Makams."

Market analysts expect the rate cut to be low, but they are divided on the possible range. Gazit said the market was expecting a cut of 0.2-0.3 percentage point from the current 15.2 percent, but Danni Shamir of Israel Discount Bank said expectations were for as much as 0.5 point.

In contrast to the rest of the market, CPI-linked bonds fell. "Inflation-linked bonds closed lower as investors took profits following the latest (price) rise," Gazit said. Shamir noted yields on the CPI long bonds had fallen sharply during the last two months.
Dollar-linked bonds rose following the sharp decline of the shekel against the dollar on Thursday, Shamir said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
